ὄφελον.g: O that! I wish! Would that!
ὄφελον.long: O that! I wish! Would that!, followed by indicative.
ὄφελον.der: first person singular of a past tense of G3784 (ὀφείλω);
ὄφελον.as:
ὄφελον, 2 aor. of ὀφείλω, without the augment (v. M, Pr., 201n), used to express a fruitless wish;
[in LXX (with aor. indic.): Ex 16:3 (מִי־יִתֵּן), Nu 14:3 (2) 20:3 (לוּא), Ps 118 (119):5 (אַחֲלֵי), etc.;]
in cl. with an infin. (chiefly poët.),
would that: with indic. aor., I Co 4:8; impf., II Co 11:1, Re 3:15; fut., Ga 5:12 (a practicable wish, v. Bl., 206 f., 220. The construction with indic. is only found in late writers.)†

ὄλεθρος.sd: a prolonged form); ruin, i.e. death, punishment
ὄλεθρος.as:
ὄλεθρος, -ον
(< ὄλλυμι, to destroy), [in LXX for שֹׁד, שָׁדַד, etc.;]
ruin, destruction, death: I Th 5:3, I Ti 6:9; αἰώνιος, II Th 1:9 (L, txt., ὀλέθριος, q.v.); εἰς ὄ. τῆς σαρκός, for physical discipline, to destroy carnal lusts, I Co 5:5.†

ὀλοθρευτής.sd: a ruiner, i.e. (specially), a venomous serpent
ὀλοθρευτής.as:
*† ὀλοθρευτής (Rec. ὁλ-), -οῦ, ὁ
(< ὀλοθρεύω),
a destroyer: I Co 10:10 (not elsewhere).†

ὁσάκις.long: as often as, as many times as.
ὁσάκις.sd: how (i.e. with G302 (ἄν), so) many times as
ὁσάκις.as:
ὁσάκις
(< ὅσος),
relat. adv., as often as: seq. ἐάν (q.v.), I Co 11:25, 26, Re 11:6.†

ὄσφρησις.as:
* ὄσφρησις, -εως, ἡ
(ὀσφραίνομαι, to smell),
the sense of smell, smelling: I Co 12:17.†

ὄφελος.der: from (to heap up, i.e. accumulate or benefit);
ὄφελος.as:
ὄφελος, -ους, τό
(< ὀφέλλω, to increase), [in LXX: Jb 15:3 (יעל hi.)*;]
advantage, help: I Co 15:32, Ja 2:14, 16.†

ὁμιλία.as:
ὁμιλία, -ας, ἡ
(< ὅμιλος), [in LXX: Ex 21:10 (עֹנָה), al.;]
company, association: I Co 15:33.†

ὀστράκινος.sd: earthen-ware, i.e. clayey; by implication, frail
ὀστράκινος.as:
ὀστράκινος-η, -ον
(< ὄστρακον, an earthen vessel or potsherd), [in LXX chiefly for חֶרֶשׂ;]
made of clay, earthen: II Co 4:7, II Ti 2:20.†

οἰκητήριον.der: neuter of a presumed derivative of G3611 (οἰκέω) (equivalent to G3612 (οἴκημα));
οἰκητήριον.as:
** οἰκητήριον, -ου, τό
(< οἰκητήρ = οἰκήτωρ, an inhabitant), [in LXX: II Mac 11:2, III Mac 2:15*;]
a habitation: Ju 6; trop., II Co 5:2.†

ὁμολογία.as:
ὁμολογία, -ας, ἡ
(< ὁμολογέω), [in LXX: De 12:6, 17, Am 4:5, Ez 46:12 (נְדָבָה), Le 22:18, Je 51 (44):25 (נֶדֶר), I Es 9:8*;]
1. in cl., an agreement, assent, compact (in π., of a contract; Deiss., BS, 249).
2.confession (prob. always in an objective sense): II Co 9:13, I Ti 6:12, 13, He 3:14:1410:13.†

ὀχύρωμα.der: from a remote derivative of G2192 (ἔχω) (meaning to fortify, through the idea of holding safely);
ὀχύρωμα.as:
ὀχύρωμα, -τος, τό
(< ὀχυρόω, to fortify, make firm), [in LXX for מִבְצָר, etc.;]
a stronghold, fortress (Ps 88 (89):40, Na 3:12, 14 al.); in LXX and NT, also metaph. of that in which confidence is placed (Pr 10:2921:22, al.): II Co 10:4.†

ὀρθοποδέω.g: I walk in a straight course, walk uprightly
ὀρθοποδέω.long: I walk in a straight course, walk uprightly.
ὀρθοποδέω.sd: to be straight-footed, i.e. (figuratively) to go directly forward
ὀρθοποδέω.der: from a compound of G3717 (ὀρθός) and G4228 (πούς);
ὀρθοποδέω.as:
*† ὀρθοποδέω, -ῶ
(< ὀρθό-πους, going straight),
= cl. εὐθυπορέω, to walk straight: metaph., Ga 2:14 (not elsewhere).†

οἰκεῖος.sd: domestic, i.e. (as noun), a relative, adherent
οἰκεῖος.as:
οἰκεῖος, -α, -ον
(< οἶκος), [in LXX for דּוֹד, שְׁאֵר, etc.; in Is 58:7, οἰ. τοῦ σπέρματος for בָּשָׂר;]
in or of the house (opp. to ξένος, ἀλλότριος);
(a) of things; τὰ οἰ., household affairs or goods;
(b) of persons, of the same family or kin; as subst., οἱ οἰ., kinsmen: I Ti 5:8; c. gen. pers., of the family of: metaph., τ. θεοῦ, Eph 2:19; τ. πίστεως (Lft., in l.), Ga 6:10.†
SYN.: συγγενής, ἴδιος (v. Cremer, 446; Deiss., BS., 123).

ὀφθαλμοδουλία.g: service rendered only while the master watches
ὀφθαλμοδουλία.long: eye-service; service rendered only while the master watches.
ὀφθαλμοδουλία.as:
*† ὀφθαλμο-δουλία (Rec. -εία), -ας, ἡ
(< ὀφθαλμός, δοῦλος),
eye-service: Eph 6:6, Col 3:22 (not found elsewhere).†

ὀκταήμερος.long: of or belonging to the eighth day, eight days old.
ὀκταήμερος.sd: an eight-day old person or act
ὀκταήμερος.as:
*† ὀκταήμερος, -ον
(< ὀκτώ, ἡμέρα),
of the eighth day, eight days old: c. dat. ref., περιτομῇ ὀ., Phl 3:5 (words of this class denote duration, cf. τεταρταῖος).†

ὁρατός.sd: gazed at, i.e. (by implication) capable of being seen

Ὀνήσιμος.long: (originally adj: useful, hence the play upon words in Philemon 10, 11, and very common as slave name), Onesimus, a slave of Philemon, a Christian of Colossae.
Ὀνήσιμος.as:
Ὀνήσιμος, -ου, ὁ
(i.e. profitable, < ὄνησις, profit),
Onesimus: Col 4:9, Phm 10 (a common name among slaves; v. MM, iii, xviii).†

ὁμείρομαι.as:
† ὀμείρομαι
(Rec. ὁμ-, v. WH, App., 151), = cl. ἱμείρομαι (but prob. with different derivation, v. Bl., § 6, 4; Zorell, s.v.), [in LXX: Jb 3:21 (חכה)*;]
to desire earnestly, yearn after: I Th 2:3.†

ὁσίως.as:
ὁσίως
(< ὅσιος),
adv.,
[in LXX: III Ki 8:61, Wi 6:10*;]
piously, holily: ὁ. καὶ δικαίως κ. ἀμέμπτως (on the distinction here between these synonyms, v. M, Th., 24 f.), I Th 2:10.†

ὀλιγόψυχος.as:
† ὀλιγόψυχος, -ον
[in LXX: Is 35:4 (מהר ni.), etc.;]
faint-hearted: I Th 5:14.†

ὁλοτελής.sd: complete to the end, i.e. absolutely perfect
ὁλοτελής.as:
*† ὁλοτελής, -ές
(< ὅλος, τέλος),
complete, perfect: I Th 5:23.†
SYN.: ὁλόκληρος (q.v.), τέλειος. "As regards meaning, ὁλόκληρος can hardly be distinguished from ὁλοτελής though, in accordance with its derivation, it draws more special attention to the several parts to which the wholeness spoken of extends, no part being wanting or lacking in completeness" (M, Th., 78).

ὁλόκληρος.g: complete in every part, sound, perfect
ὁλόκληρος.long: complete in every part, sound, perfect, entire.
ὁλόκληρος.sd: complete in every part, i.e. perfectly sound (in body)
ὁλόκληρος.as:
ὁλό-κληρος, -ον
(< ὅλος, κλῆρος, i.e. with all that has fallen by lot), [in LXX: Le 23:15, Ez 15:5 (תָּמִים), De 27:6, Jos 9:2 (8:31) (שָׁלֵם), Za 11:16 (נצב ni.), Wi 15:3, I Mac 4:47, IV Mac 15:17*;]
complete, entire; in NT in ethical sense (as Wi 15:3, IV Mac 15:17), I Th 5:23; ὁ. καὶ τέλειοι, Ja 1:4.†
SYN.: ὁλοτελής (q.v.), τέλειος (Tr., Syn., § xxii).

ὀρέγομαι.long: I stretch forth, mid: I hanker after, long for, am eager for, aspire to.
ὀρέγομαι.sd: to stretch oneself, i.e. reach out after (long for)
ὀρέγομαι.der: middle voice of apparently a prolonged form of an obsolete primary (compare G3735 (ὄρος));
ὀρέγομαι.as:
** ὀρέγω,
[in Sm.: Jb 8:20, Ez 16:49*;]
to reach, stretch out; pass. and mid., to stretch oneself out, reach forth; metaph., to reach after, grasp at, aspire to: c. gen. rei, I Ti 3:1, He 11:16; φιλαργυρίας (v. Ellic. and CGT, in l.), I Ti 6:10.†
SYN.: ἐπιθυμέω, to desire (q.v.).

ὁμολογουμένως.der: adverb of present passive participle of G3670 (ὁμολογέω);
ὁμολογουμένως.as:
** ὁμολογουμένως,
adv.
(< ὁμολογέω), [in LXX: IV Mac 6:317:1616:1*;]
1.as agreed, conformably with.
2.confessedly, by common consent: I Ti 3:16.†

οἰκοδεσποτέω.sd: to be the head of (i.e. rule) a family
οἰκοδεσποτέω.as:
οἰκο-δεσποτέω, -ῶ
(< οἰκοδεσπότης),
to rule a household: I Ti 5:14.†

Ὀνησίφορος.long: Onesiphorus, a Christian of the province of Asia.
Ὀνησίφορος.der: from a derivative of G3685 (ὀνίνημι) and G5411 (φόρος);
Ὀνησίφορος.as:
Ὀνησίφορος, -ου, ὁ
(i.e. bringing advantage),
Onesiphorus: II Ti 1:164:19.†

ὀρθοτομέω.long: I cut straight; met: I handle correctly, teach rightly.
ὀρθοτομέω.der: from a compound of G3717 (ὀρθός) and the base of G5114 (τομώτερος), to make a straight cut, i.e. (figuratively) to dissect (expound) correctly (the divine message)
ὀρθοτομέω.as:
† ὀρθοτομέω, -ῶ
(< ὀρθός, τέμνω), [in LXX: Pr 3:611:6 (ישׁר pi.)*;]
to cut straight, as a road (τ. ὁδούς, fig., Pr 3:611:6). Metaph., τ. λόγον τ. ἀληθείας, II Ti 2:15 (V. Ellic. and CGT, in l.; not found elsewhere).†

ὀργίλος.as:
ὀργίλος, -η, -ον
(< ὀργή), [in LXX: Pr 22:2429:22 (חֵמָה), etc.;]
inclined to anger, passionate: Tit 1:7.†

οἰκουργός.as:
*† οἰκουργός, -όν
(< οἶκος + root of ἔργον),
working at home: Tit 2:5 (Rec. οἰκουρός, q.v.).†

ὀνίνημι.g: I help, profit, have joy of
ὀνίνημι.long: I profit, benefit, help; mid: I have profit, derive benefit.
ὀνίνημι.sd: for which another prolonged form () is used as an alternate in some tenses (unless indeed it be identical with the base of G3686 (ὄνομα) through the idea of notoriety); to gratify, i.e. (middle voice) to derive pleasure or advantage from
ὀνίνημι.der: a prolonged form of an apparently primary verb (, to slur);
ὀνίνημι.as:
** ὀνίνημι,
[in LXX: To 3:8, Si 30:2*;]
to profit, benefit, help; mid., to have profit, derive benefit: optat. (M, Pr., 195), c. gen., Phm 20.†

ὁμοιότης.as:
ὁμοιότης, -ητος, ἡ
(< ὅμοιος), [in LXX: Ge 1:11, 12 (מִין), Wi 14:19, IV Mac 15:4*;]
likeness: καθ’ ὁμοιότητα, in like manner, He 4:15; id. c. gen. (MM, xviii), after the likeness (of), He 7:15.†

ὁρκωμοσία.g: the taking of an oath, an oath
ὁρκωμοσία.long: the taking of an oath, an oath.
ὁρκωμοσία.der: from a compound of G3727 (ὅρκος) and a derivative of G3660 (ὀμνύω);
ὁρκωμοσία.as:
ὁρκωμοσία, -ας, ἡ
(< ὅρκος, ὄμνυμι; by metapl. for τὰ ὁρκωμόσια, asseverations on oath; v. MM, xviii), [in LXX: Ez 17:18, 19 (אָלָה) I Es 9:93*;]
affirmation on oath, an oath: He 7:20, 21, 28.†

ὀλοθρεύω.as:
† ὀλοθρεύω
(< ὄλεθρος), late (Alex.) form of ὄλεθρεύω (cf. MGr., ξολοθρεύω), [in LXX for כּרת, שׁחת hi., etc.;]
to destroy: He 11:28 (cf. ἐξ-ολοθρεύω).†

ὀπή.long: a crevice (in a rock), a cave, an opening, hole.
ὀπή.sd: a hole (as if for light), i.e. cavern; by analogy, a spring (of water)
ὀπή.as:
ὀπή, -ῆς, ἡ,
[in LXX for חֹר, חָגוּ, etc.;]
an opening, a hole: Ja 3:11 (cf. Ex 33:22), He 11:33 (cf. Ob 3).†

ὄγκος.long: (properly: bulk, mass, hence) a weight, burden, encumbrance.
ὄγκος.sd: a mass (as bending or bulging by its load), i.e. burden (hindrance)
ὄγκος.der: probably from the same as G43 (ἀγκάλη);
ὄγκος.as:
* ὄγκος, -ου, ὁ,
bulk, mass; metaph., an encumbrance: He 12:1.†
SYN.: βάρος, a weight; φορτίον, a burden, that which is borne.

ὀλιγωρέω.long: I despise, hold in low esteem, make light of.
ὀλιγωρέω.sd: to have little regard for, i.e. to disesteem
ὀλιγωρέω.der: from a compound of G3641 (ὀλίγος) and ("care");
ὀλιγωρέω.as:
ὀλιγωρέω, -ῶ
(< ὀλίγος + ὤρα, care), [in LXX: Pr 3:11 (מאס)*;]
to esteem lightly, think little of: c. gen., He 12:5(LXX).†

ὁμοίωσις.as:
ὁμοίωσις, -εως, ἡ
(ὁμοιόω), [in LXX chiefly for דְּמוּת, Ps 57 (58):4, al.;]
1.a making like, becoming like (Plat.).
2.likeness: Ja 3:9(LXX).†
SYN.: v.s. ὁμοίωμα, and cf. Tr., Syn., § xv.

ὀλολύζω.long: I howl, lament loudly, cry aloud, bewail.
ὀλολύζω.as:
ὀλολύζω
(onomatop.), [in LXX chiefly for ילל hi.;] (in Hom., of women crying to the gods in prayer or thanksgiving),
to cry aloud: Ja 5:1.†

ὄψιμος.as:
ὄψιμος, -ον
(< ὀψέ), [in LXX: De 11:14, Pr 16:15, Ho 6:4 (3), Jl 2:23, Za 10:1, Je 5:24 (מַלְקוֹשׁ), Ex 9:32 (אָפִיל)*;] poët. and late for ὄψιος,
late: ὑετὸς ὄ., the latter rain (v. DB, s.v. "rain"), with ellipsis of ὑετός (v. WM, 740), Ja 5:7.†

ὁμόφρων.der: from the base of G3674 (ὁμοῦ) and G5424 (φρήν);
ὁμόφρων.as:
* ὁμόφρων, -ον
(< ὁμός, φρήν), = ὁμόνοος,
agreeing, of one mind: I Pe 3:8.†

ὁπλίζομαι.sd: to equip (with weapons (middle voice and figuratively))
ὁπλίζομαι.as:
** ὁπλίζω
(< ὅπλον), [in Sm.: Je 52:25*;]
to make ready, equip; of soldiers, to arm. Mid., to arm oneself; fig., ἔννοιαν: I Pe 4:1 (cf. θράσος ὁ., Soph., Elec., 995), (cf. καθ-οπλίζω).†

οἰνοφλυγία.sd: an overflow (or surplus) of wine, i.e. vinolency (drunkenness)
οἰνοφλυγία.der: from G3631 (οἶνος) and a form of the base of G5397 (φλύαρος);
οἰνοφλυγία.as:
* οἰνοφλυγία, -ας, ἡ
(< φλύω, to bubble up, overflow), cf. -γέω, De 21:20;
drunkenness, debauchery: I Pe 4:3.†
SYN.: v.s. κραιπάλη.

ὁμίχλη.as:
ὁμίχλη, -ης, ἡ,
[in LXX for עֲרָפֶל, etc.;]
a mist: II Pe 2:17.†
SYN.: νέφος, νεφέλη, both thicker than ὁ.

ὀλίγως.as:
ὀλίγως, adv.
(< ὀλίγος), [in Aq.: Is 10:7*;]
a little, almost, all but: II Pe 2:18.†

ὄλυνθος.long: an unripe fig, one which, not ripening in due time, grows through the winter and falls off in the spring.
ὄλυνθος.sd: an unripe (because out of season) fig
ὄλυνθος.as:
ὄλυνθος, -ου, ὁ,
[in LXX: Ca 2:13 (פַּגָּה)*;]
an unripe fig, which grows in winter and usually falls off in the spring: Re 6:13.†

οὐρά.as:
οὐρά, -ᾶς, ἡ,
[in LXX for זָנָב;]
a tail: Re 9:10, 1912:4.†

ὄρνεον.der: neuter of a presumed derivative of G3733 (ὄρνις);
ὄρνεον.as:
ὄρνεον, -ου, τό, = ὄρνις,
[in LXX chiefly for צִפּוֹר;]
a bird: Re 18:219:17, 21 (Hom., al.).†

ὀπώρα.sd: properly, even-tide of the (summer) season (dog-days), i.e. (by implication) ripe fruit
ὀπώρα.der: apparently from the base of G3796 (ὀψέ) and G5610 (ὥρα);
ὀπώρα.as:
ὀπώρα, -ας, ἡ,
[in LXX: Je 31 (48):3247 (40):10, 12 (קַיִץ)*;]
1.late summer, early autumn (the time between the risings of Sirius and Arcturus, i.e. late July, all August and early September).
2. By meton. (as being fruit-time), ripe fruitsRe 18:14 (cf. φθινοπωρινά, Ju 12).†

ὅρμημα.as:
ὅρμημα, -τος, τό
(ὁρμάω), [in LXX: Ho 5:10, Am 1:11 (עֶבְרָה), etc.;]
a rush: Re 18:21.†
